completar.title: Complete your retirement plan
completar.text: Without the year you want to stop and the income you want, we can’t calculate the effect of each choice.

reserva.title: Save {amount} in your emergency fund
reserva.text: The emergency fund comes first: it keeps you from using expensive credit when something unexpected happens.

divida.title: Pay {amount} more on your most expensive debt
divida.text: The interest on this debt costs more than your money earns. Once it’s paid off, the amount goes to your plan.

guardar.title: Save {amount} more per month
guardar.text: This amount goes into your retirement plan and starts earning dividends.

gasto.title: Cut {amount} from {category}
gasto.text: That’s 10% of your largest category last month. Saving the difference also shortens the path.

reserva.title: Emergency fund
reserva.description: Money set aside for the unexpected, like a loss of income or a repair, so you don’t have to go into debt.

errors.contribution: Enter how much to save per month like 500.00.
errors.accountGone: This account is no longer available.

essential.intro: This is what your family needs to live for a month: housing, groceries, bills and transportation.
essential.label: Essential expenses per month (R$)
essential.hint: Optional. If left blank, we calculate it from transactions in essential categories.

need.title: How much I need to save
need.unknownTitle: We still need your essential expenses
need.unknownText: The size of your emergency fund depends on how much your family spends each month on what can’t be cut. With that number, we calculate the rest.
need.summary: {count, plural, =1 {# month} other {# months}} of your essential expenses, at {amount} per month.

basis.average: {months, plural, =1 {Based on your expenses in the last closed month.} other {Based on your average expenses over the last # months.}}
basis.estimate: This is an estimate based on the current month, including what’s planned.

have.title: How much I already have
have.status: {count, plural, =0 {No account selected yet.} =1 {Kept in {name}.} other {Kept in # accounts.}}
have.text: Your emergency fund is the balance of the accounts selected below. The whole account counts, so it’s best to use an account just for this.
have.emptyTitle: You don’t have any accounts yet
have.emptyText: Add the account where you keep this money so it shows up here.

missing.title: How much is left
missing.unknownText: As soon as we know your essential expenses, we’ll show how much is left and how long it will take you to get there.
missing.progress: {percent} of the goal · covers {count, plural, =1 {# month} other {# months}} of essential expenses
missing.forecast: Saving {amount} per month, you’ll get there in {date}, {count, plural, =1 {# month} other {# months}} from now.

contribution.label: How much I can save per month (R$)
contribution.saveLabel: Save how much to set aside per month

markEssential.title: Mark what’s essential
markEssential.text: You already have expenses logged, but none in an essential category. Mark housing, groceries, bills and anything else you can’t cut as essential.

logExpenses.title: Log this month’s expenses
logExpenses.text: To calculate your emergency fund, we need to know how much housing, groceries and bills cost. Log these expenses, or enter the total amount above.

complete.title: Your emergency fund is complete
complete.text: Keep this money set aside and top it up whenever you use it. What you save from now on can go to your goals.

completeExtra.title: Your emergency fund is complete
completeExtra.text: You have {amount} more than you need. This surplus can go to your goals. Keep the rest set aside and top it up whenever you use it.

createAccount.title: Create the emergency fund account
createAccount.text: Your emergency fund lives in one of your accounts. Create an account to keep this money and then select it here.

chooseAccount.title: Choose where your emergency fund is kept
chooseAccount.text: Select the account where you keep this money. If you don’t have a separate one yet, it’s worth creating one just for this.

setAmount.title: Decide how much to save per month
setAmount.text: Pick an amount that fits your month, even a small one. Then we can show when your emergency fund will be ready.

saveOne.title: Save {amount} this month
saveOne.text: Put this amount in {place}. Repeat every month until your emergency fund is complete.

saveMany.title: Save {amount} this month
saveMany.text: Put this amount in one of your emergency fund accounts. Repeat every month until your emergency fund is complete.

how.title: How it works
how.source: Where essential expenses come from. We add up everything you logged in categories marked as essential, including card purchases and debt installments. We use the average of the last 3 closed months. If you’re just getting started, you’ll see an estimate based on the current month, and you can enter the amount if you prefer.
how.mark: How to mark a category as essential. In Categories, edit the category and check “This is an essential expense”. From then on, expenses in that category count toward the calculation.
how.money: How money gets into the emergency fund. The emergency fund isn’t a new account: it adds up the balance of the accounts you select here. If the balance goes up or down, the fund follows.

patrimonio.description: What you own minus what you owe.

quote.waiting: The automatic price arrives at the next update.

portfolio.description: What everything you recorded is worth today.

empty.title: Your portfolio starts here
empty.text: Add stocks, funds, fixed income or private pensions. The value goes into your net worth. If you already keep this money in an investment account in the system, use only one of the two.

portfolio.oversold: There is a sale larger than the position. Check the trades.
portfolio.estimated: No current value: showing the cost.
portfolio.disclaimer: Stocks, FIIs (Brazilian real estate funds), ETFs (exchange-traded funds) and BDRs (Brazilian receipts for foreign stocks) with a valid ticker get automatic prices, updated after the B3 (Brazilian stock exchange) closes and always delayed. Everything else is entered by you. OrganizeUp organizes and compares, and does not recommend buying or selling investments. See also <link>dividends</link>.

remove.title: Delete investment
remove.text: "{name}" leaves the portfolio, along with its trades and dividends.

investmentForm.codeHint: E.g. PETR4, HGLG11. For stocks, real estate funds, ETFs and BDRs, this is what brings in the price and dividends on their own.

valueForm.hintAuto: Valid until the next automatic quote.

trades.title: Transactions
trades.description: Everything that went in and out of the portfolio.

empty.title: No trades yet
empty.text: Add an investment in Portfolio and the purchases show up here.

trades.balanceHint: Buys minus sells in the trades below.

remove.title: Delete trade
remove.text: The position and average price will be recalculated. If the trade took money from an account, the account transaction goes with it.

rebalance.title: Rebalancing
rebalance.description: Compare your portfolio with the split you chose.

empty.title: No portfolio to compare yet
empty.text: Add an investment and set how much you want in each class.

next.title: If you contribute now
next.description: Shows how to bring your portfolio closer to your targets without selling anything.
next.noneBelow: No class with a target is below it.
next.leftover: {amount} left over: the classes are already on target.

noTargets.title: Set your targets
noTargets.text: Say how much you want in each class to see the difference and split your next contribution.

rebalance.disclaimer: Comparison with the targets you set. Educational content, not an investment recommendation.

form.title: Targets by class
form.intro: Say how much of your portfolio you want in each class. The decision is yours: the system only compares and does not point to any asset.
